t: Lesson 5, connectors. Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
Let's plug the agent into the tools you already use.
Copying and pasting data into a chat goes stale the moment you do it.
A connector lets the agent read live data and take real actions.
The standard is called MCP, the Model Context Protocol.
It gives the agent live data from your docs, tickets, and code.
It lets the agent take real actions, like creating, updating, and sending.
And it works the same way across harnesses.
Setting one up takes three things. A name and a command to start the server.
And a key, keep the key in an environment variable. Never paste it into the file.
Give the least access that works. Start read only, use scope tokens,
and require approval for anything that writes or sends.
Quick recap, MCP gives your agent live data and real actions through one standard.
Your mission, connect one tool you use every day, read only, and ask the agent a question about it.
Your agent can now reach real work. Next, we turn repeat requests into one-word commands.
